messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The walls are cracking, but no one’s sure if it’s the whole thing coming down or just the paint peeling off—either way, the air feels different. Keep your heads down, but maybe start thinking about where you’d rather be if the wind changes."*"
Sender 2: "*"The walls are cracking—leadership is turning on itself, the streets are humming with something new, and even the usual sources are lost. We’re not just watching the storm anymore; we’re in it. Stay sharp, stay ready, and keep your circles tight."*"
Sender 3: "*"The air feels different now—like the ground’s shifting under us, but no one’s sure if it’s an earthquake or just the first cracks. The usual checks and balances are fraying, and the jokes in the market aren’t just jokes anymore. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this could be the calm before the storm, or the storm itself. Let’s talk in person soon."*"
Sender 4: "*"The walls are cracking—everyone can see it now. The question isn’t *if* things will change, but *how fast* and whether we’re ready when it happens. Let’s keep our heads down but our eyes open—no sudden moves, just quiet preparation."*"
Sender 5: "*"The walls are cracking—you can hear it in the way people talk now, like they’re already halfway to believing things could be different. But the real question isn’t if, it’s how fast, and whether the ones with the guns will still be listening to the same orders by then. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t a race, it’s a collapse, and we don’t want to be the ones standing in the wrong place when it happens."*"
Sender 6: "*"The walls are cracking—quietly, but you can feel the draft. The regime’s still putting on a show, but the backstage is chaos, and the audience is starting to whisper. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time to trip over our own feet."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are cracking—you can hear it in the quiet. The usual signs are there, but the real tell is how the old guard is suddenly *too* calm, like they’re holding their breath. Keep your plans fluid, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time to be the first to move."*"
Sender 8: "*"The walls are cracking—even the usual watchdogs are looking the other way. The question isn’t if, but when, and the smart money’s already betting on how fast things unravel. Keep your heads down, but be ready—this isn’t just talk anymore."*"
Sender 9: "*"The walls are cracking—even the ones who should be holding them up are looking the other way. Keep your ears open, but don’t let anyone see you listening too closely."*"
Sender 10: "*"The walls are cracking—people are talking differently now, even the ones who used to whisper. The regime’s scrambling, but no one’s sure if the silence from the top is weakness or a trap. Stay sharp, but keep your eyes open—this could move fast."*"
Sender 11: "*"The air feels different—like the ground’s shifting under us, but no one’s admitting it yet. The usual cracks are gone, but that’s not a good sign—it’s like they’re all holding their breath, waiting to see who blinks first. Stay sharp, but don’t make any moves yet. We’ll talk soon."*"
Sender 12: "*"The air feels different now—like everyone’s quietly packing their bags, not just complaining. The usual cracks are showing, but the real question is whether the guards at the gates will still be there when the time comes. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t a drill."*"
Sender 13: "*"The walls are cracking—more than we thought. The usual watchdogs are distracted, the markets are steady, and even the tea house crowd is talking like it’s 1989 again. But the real question isn’t *if* things are moving—it’s whether the guns will still answer when the order comes. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for safety."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are cracking—more than just paint flaking off. The guards at the checkpoints are whispering to each other instead of watching the road, and the usual threats aren’t coming. Even the ones who used to scream the loudest are just staring at their shoes now. We’re not talking about ‘when’ anymore—just how fast it unravels, and whether they’ll try to burn it all down before they go."*"
Sender 15: "*"The ship’s drifting—no one’s at the wheel, and the crew’s starting to notice. The usual rules don’t apply anymore, but that doesn’t mean we’re safe. Let’s talk soon, but carefully."*"
Sender 16: "*"The air feels different now—like the ground’s shifting underfoot, but no one’s admitting they feel it too. The usual signs are there, but the quiet ones are louder: the ones who always knew everything suddenly don’t, the ones who never missed a chance to speak now say nothing, and the streets? They’re acting like nothing’s wrong. That’s the part that worries me."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are cracking—quietly, but fast. The old hands are stepping back, the money’s slipping away, and even the censors have stopped pretending. No one’s saying it out loud yet, but the air feels different—like the moment before the dam breaks. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. The right move now is to be ready, not to be seen."*"
Sender 18: "*"The walls are cracking—people are talking louder, the regime’s messages sound like they’re for themselves, not us, and even the loyalists are asking about exit plans. Something’s coming, but no one’s sure if it’ll be a storm or a slow unraveling. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and keep your bags packed—just in case."*"
Sender 19: "*"The walls are cracking—even the generals are whispering now. Keep your heads down, but be ready: the wind’s shifting, and no one knows yet if it’s a storm or just the calm before the knife comes out."*"
Sender 20: "*"The walls are cracking—not just in the corners, but all at once. The teachers’ slowdowns, the payments still coming, the journalist’s pieces going unpunished—it’s not just us seeing it. Even the officers are waiting for orders now. Stay sharp, but don’t assume the worst is coming. It might already be here."*"
Sender 21: "*"The walls are cracking—no one’s bothering to patch them anymore. The shopkeeper on 5th Street said it best: ‘Something has to give.’ Stay sharp, but don’t rush. The old rules are gone, but the new ones aren’t written yet."*"
Sender 22: "*"The air feels different now—like the ground’s shifting underfoot, and not just for us. Even the ones who used to whisper in corners are talking like it’s already happening. But the real question isn’t *if*, it’s *how*—and whether the ones with the guns are still waiting for orders or just waiting for the right moment to pick a side. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet. The walls have ears, and the floor might give way."*"
Sender 23: "*"The walls are cracking—even the shopkeepers are talking openly now, and the usual noise from the regime’s bots sounds like a broken radio. The question isn’t *if* things are coming apart, but how fast, and whether anyone outside will step in before it’s too late. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—we’ll know soon enough."*"
Sender 24: "*"The air feels different now—like the moment before a storm breaks. The cracks are showing, and people are starting to move, not just whisper. Let’s stay sharp, but keep our heads down—this could go fast, and we don’t know who’s still holding the strings."*"
Sender 25: "*"The walls are cracking—even the loyalists are whispering, and the soldiers at the checkpoints don’t look like they’re ready to shoot their own neighbors. The regime’s still screaming the same script, but the whole thing feels like a stage play with the audience walking out mid-act. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could go either way fast."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
